result:
Round 266 is implemented and there is no STOP. Ctrl+E on a time selection that crosses a clip edge splits the clip again, as it did before round 265. The report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-266.md`.

**What changed (only the 7 granted files):**
- **Split rule D3 (`model.ts`):** `splitClipsByRange` now cuts every clip on the selection's lane that overlaps the selection, but only at selection edges that fall inside a clip. The parts inside the selection are returned in timeline order. It returns nothing when no cut happens.
- **`ArrangementContext.tsx` (range branch only):** one part keeps the old behaviour and text. Two or more parts are all selected and get the new status `splitRangeClipsDone(n)`. A refusal keeps the selection and adds no Undo step; a split adds one.
- **Copy (`strings.ts`):** the export dialog and Ctrl+L messages now say "drag in a lane".
- **Tests:** the old `middleId` test was rewritten without dropping any assertion. ST1, ST7, ST8 and ST10 are updated. I added MS1–MS7 and BS1–BS4; BT1–BT9 are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Doc 198:** line 4 now reads "C round 266 PASS", and the sections describe D3, the copy change and the C-R265-01 fix.

**Checks I actually ran:**
- typecheck and lint pass, with no new lint warnings compared with round 265. Scoped Biome passes.
- The 9 targeted test files pass (218 tests). The slowest row is about 1 s against the 5 s limit.
- The frozen-file check returns rc 0 before and after. Git status shows 16 entries, every edit is inside the allowed line ranges, and HEAD is still `2ea196e`.
- **Mutants:** M6–M9 all fail the tests as required. I added two of my own mutants (M10, M11), and both fail too. A third (M12) passes because it doesn't change behaviour, and I recorded it that way rather than counting it.
- **Browser:** I ran B's probe on :5173 at both viewports. All 23 readings match B's sketch values exactly, with 0 page errors. This is my own check, not C's acceptance.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer found no correctness bug. I added the missing tests it pointed to (MS6, MS7 and an overlay check in BS1/BS4) and fixed two doc claims.

**For B to rule on:**
- **Sort order:** I sort the clips by start time, where B's sketch kept the array's own order. This decides which part becomes the primary selection.
- **"Both edges" text (B-R266-1):** the existing split status and button title say "both edges" even when only one edge was cut. This was already true at HEAD; C's own capture `c-round-265/nb-head.json` (`pastStartSplit`) shows it. The task kept that text unchanged, so I didn't touch it.
- **Architecture note:** the reviewer suggests keeping `splitSelection` as it is. If one more split variant arrives, it suggests a small function in `lib/arrangement/` that maps a split result to the selection and status.

**Not done:** I didn't run the full suite, `verify`, the build or e2e; those belong to the gate under the speed rules. All of C's browser rows are still to run. Nothing is marked complete in the backlog.
